items.title: Splitting the defining polynomials of a finite algebra after a finite free base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that after a finite free ring extension, a finite algebra becomes a quotient of a polynomial ring by monic polynomials that split completely into linear factors. The proof chooses generators of the algebra over the ring, picks a monic polynomial for each generator annihilating it, and then applies the adjoining-a-root lemma once for each linear factor required, which produces a finite free extension in which all the polynomials split. Mapping the variables to the generators realises the algebra as a quotient of the polynomial ring modulo the now split polynomials.
